blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.45

blocks.text: भूयः स्यात्प्रतिमीलनम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] भूयः स्यात्प्रतिमीलनम्

blocks.text: Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.
blocks.directed: Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.

blocks.text: Again and again, there is the complete reunion of inward and outward awareness in the supreme Self.
blocks.directed: Again and again, there is the complete reunion of inward and outward awareness in the supreme Self.

blocks.text: The Greatest Plot Twist: You Were Śiva the Entire Bloody Time.
blocks.directed: The Greatest Plot Twist: You Were Śiva the Entire Bloody Time.

blocks.text: And that’s it.
blocks.directed: And that’s it.

blocks.text: The final sūtra.
blocks.directed: The final sūtra.

blocks.text: The seventy-seventh statement.
blocks.directed: The seventy-seventh statement.

blocks.text: Vasugupta has spent the entire text explaining the nature of consciousness, the structure of bondage, the powers of Śakti, and the means of liberation.
blocks.directed: Vasugupta has spent the entire text explaining the nature of consciousness, the structure of bondage, the powers of Śakti, and the means of liberation.

blocks.text: And he ends with:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And he ends with:

blocks.text: Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.

blocks.text: Now we need to be exceptionally careful with this one.
blocks.directed: Now we need to be exceptionally careful with this one.

blocks.text: Because the word pratimīlana is doing enormous philosophical work.
blocks.directed: Because the word pratimīlana is doing enormous philosophical work.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Bhūyaḥ — again, repeatedly, abundantly.
blocks.directed: Bhūyaḥ — again, repeatedly, abundantly.

blocks.text: Syāt — may be, should be, comes to be.
blocks.directed: Syāt — may be, should be, comes to be.

blocks.text: Pratimīlanam — closing together, folding together, reunion or complete integration.
blocks.directed: Pratimīlanam — closing together, folding together, reunion or complete integration.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja gives it a very particular interpretation.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja gives it a very particular interpretation.

blocks.text: He connects pratimīlana with two complementary movements.
blocks.directed: He connects pratimīlana with two complementary movements.

blocks.text: Nimīlana.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Nimīlana.

blocks.text: Closing inward.
blocks.directed: Closing inward.

blocks.text: The withdrawal of consciousness from differentiated manifestation into its own nature.
blocks.directed: The withdrawal of consciousness from differentiated manifestation into its own nature.

blocks.text: And:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And:

blocks.text: Unmīlana.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Unmīlana.

blocks.text: Opening outward.
blocks.directed: Opening outward.

blocks.text: The manifestation of the universe through that same consciousness.
blocks.directed: The manifestation of the universe through that same consciousness.

blocks.text: Now think about what that means.
blocks.directed: Now think about what that means.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, spiritual practice can appear to involve a movement away from the world.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, spiritual practice can appear to involve a movement away from the world.

blocks.text: You withdraw.
blocks.directed: You withdraw.

blocks.text: You close your eyes.
blocks.directed: You close your eyes.

blocks.text: You turn attention inward.
blocks.directed: You turn attention inward.

blocks.text: You seek the source.
blocks.directed: You seek the source.

blocks.text: And in some traditions, that inward withdrawal becomes the principal image of liberation.
blocks.directed: And in some traditions, that inward withdrawal becomes the principal image of liberation.

blocks.text: But Trika gives us something more comprehensive.
blocks.directed: But Trika gives us something more comprehensive.

blocks.text: Because the supreme reality isn’t merely a state of withdrawal.
blocks.directed: Because the supreme reality isn’t merely a state of withdrawal.

blocks.text: Śiva possesses the freedom of manifestation.
blocks.directed: Śiva possesses the freedom of manifestation.

blocks.text: And therefore the outward opening is not ultimately separate from the inward source.
blocks.directed: And therefore the outward opening is not ultimately separate from the inward source.

blocks.text: Nimīlana and unmīlana are not two different absolute realities.
blocks.directed: Nimīlana and unmīlana are not two different absolute realities.

blocks.text: They’re complementary movements of one consciousness.
blocks.directed: They’re complementary movements of one consciousness.

blocks.text: And pratimīlana is the integration of both.
blocks.directed: And pratimīlana is the integration of both.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja’s explanation is extraordinary.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja’s explanation is extraordinary.

blocks.text: He says the universe arises from the essential nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: He says the universe arises from the essential nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: Then, for the yogi established in supreme yoga, the universe is folded back into that conscious reality.
blocks.directed: Then, for the yogi established in supreme yoga, the universe is folded back into that conscious reality.

blocks.text: But this doesn’t necessarily mean the physical world disappears.
blocks.directed: But this doesn’t necessarily mean the physical world disappears.

blocks.text: The crucial movement is the disappearance of the residual impression of duality.
blocks.directed: The crucial movement is the disappearance of the residual impression of duality.

blocks.text: Bhedasaṃskāra.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Bhedasaṃskāra.

blocks.text: The latent impression of difference.
blocks.directed: The latent impression of difference.

blocks.text: That impression falls away.
blocks.directed: That impression falls away.

blocks.text: And the yogi recognises the universe as not fundamentally separate from consciousness.
blocks.directed: And the yogi recognises the universe as not fundamentally separate from consciousness.

blocks.text: Now here’s the beautiful thing.
blocks.directed: Now here’s the beautiful thing.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explains that the inward closing and outward opening become aspects of the same supreme recognition.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explains that the inward closing and outward opening become aspects of the same supreme recognition.

blocks.text: When awareness is directed inward, the yogi recognises consciousness.
blocks.directed: When awareness is directed inward, the yogi recognises consciousness.

blocks.text: When the universe appears outwardly, the yogi recognises that appearance as the manifestation of consciousness.
blocks.directed: When the universe appears outwardly, the yogi recognises that appearance as the manifestation of consciousness.

blocks.text: The distinction between inward and outward no longer conceals their fundamental unity.
blocks.directed: The distinction between inward and outward no longer conceals their fundamental unity.

blocks.text: And this is precisely why pratimīlana is such a perfect ending.
blocks.directed: And this is precisely why pratimīlana is such a perfect ending.

blocks.text: Because the entire text has been concerned with the relation between the Self and manifestation.
blocks.directed: Because the entire text has been concerned with the relation between the Self and manifestation.

blocks.text: At the beginning:
blocks.directed: [short pause] At the beginning:

blocks.text: चैतन्यमात्मा।
blocks.directed: [slowly] चैतन्यमात्मा।

blocks.text: Caitanyam ātmā.
blocks.directed: Caitanyam ātmā.

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: Then:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Then:

blocks.text: ज्ञानं बन्धः।
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानं बन्धः।

blocks.text: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.

blocks.text: Limited knowledge is bondage.
blocks.directed: Limited knowledge is bondage.

blocks.text: And now, at the end:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And now, at the end:

blocks.text: भूयः स्यात्प्रतिमीलनम्।
blocks.directed: [slowly] भूयः स्यात्प्रतिमीलनम्।

blocks.text: Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Bhūyaḥ syāt pratimīlanam.

blocks.text: Repeated integration into the supreme conscious reality.
blocks.directed: Repeated integration into the supreme conscious reality.

blocks.text: The apparent separation between subject and object has been overcome.
blocks.directed: The apparent separation between subject and object has been overcome.

blocks.text: But not through the permanent annihilation of the world.
blocks.directed: But not through the permanent annihilation of the world.

blocks.text: Rather, through recognition of the world as the manifestation of the Self.
blocks.directed: Rather, through recognition of the world as the manifestation of the Self.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja makes the central point absolutely explicit.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja makes the central point absolutely explicit.

blocks.text: He says the yogi’s Śiva-nature is not something new.
blocks.directed: He says the yogi’s Śiva-nature is not something new.

blocks.text: Nāpūrvam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Nāpūrvam.

blocks.text: Not newly produced.
blocks.directed: Not newly produced.

blocks.text: Rather:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Rather:

blocks.text: Svabhāva eva.
blocks.directed: Svabhāva eva.

blocks.text: It is their own essential nature.
blocks.directed: It is their own essential nature.

blocks.text: And this is the ultimate revelation.
blocks.directed: And this is the ultimate revelation.

blocks.text: The yogi doesn’t become Śiva by creating an entirely new metaphysical identity.
blocks.directed: The yogi doesn’t become Śiva by creating an entirely new metaphysical identity.

blocks.text: The yogi recognises the Śiva-nature that was always fundamental.
blocks.directed: The yogi recognises the Śiva-nature that was always fundamental.

blocks.text: Māyā had obscured it through the power of differentiated mental construction.
blocks.directed: Māyā had obscured it through the power of differentiated mental construction.

blocks.text: The practitioner had experienced themselves as limited.
blocks.directed: The practitioner had experienced themselves as limited.

blocks.text: The body appeared to define the Self.
blocks.directed: The body appeared to define the Self.

blocks.text: The senses appeared to encounter a separate world.
blocks.directed: The senses appeared to encounter a separate world.

blocks.text: The mind became absorbed in differentiated cognition.
blocks.directed: The mind became absorbed in differentiated cognition.

blocks.text: Desire produced the movement outward.
blocks.directed: Desire produced the movement outward.

blocks.text: And the individual wandered through conditioned existence.
blocks.directed: And the individual wandered through conditioned existence.

blocks.text: But the supreme nature of consciousness had never ceased to be the reality underlying the entire process.
blocks.directed: But the supreme nature of consciousness had never ceased to be the reality underlying the entire process.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja explicitly says that the methods described throughout the work serve to reveal this already-existing Śiva-nature.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja explicitly says that the methods described throughout the work serve to reveal this already-existing Śiva-nature.

blocks.text: Not manufacture it.
blocks.directed: Not manufacture it.

blocks.text: Reveal it.
blocks.directed: Reveal it.

blocks.text: And now comes a magnificent metaphor from the Svacchandatantra, quoted by Kṣemarāja.
blocks.directed: And now comes a magnificent metaphor from the Svacchandatantra, quoted by Kṣemarāja.

blocks.text: The image is of fire.
blocks.directed: The image is of fire.

blocks.text: Fire emerging from wood.
blocks.directed: Fire emerging from wood.

blocks.text: Once kindled, the fire becomes brilliantly luminous.
blocks.directed: Once kindled, the fire becomes brilliantly luminous.

blocks.text: And the liberated Self is compared to this emergence.
blocks.directed: And the liberated Self is compared to this emergence.

blocks.text: The fire isn’t created as an entirely alien substance imposed from outside.
blocks.directed: The fire isn’t created as an entirely alien substance imposed from outside.

blocks.text: The analogy is used to explain the disclosure of a nature previously concealed by limiting conditions.
blocks.directed: The analogy is used to explain the disclosure of a nature previously concealed by limiting conditions.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja cites the Svacchandatantra on the yogi who has become free from the impurities and limiting powers.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja cites the Svacchandatantra on the yogi who has become free from the impurities and limiting powers.

blocks.text: Even while remaining within manifestation, the liberated person is no longer bound by it in the former manner.
blocks.directed: Even while remaining within manifestation, the liberated person is no longer bound by it in the former manner.

blocks.text: Then he concludes the entire commentary by explaining the final sūtra’s deepest point.
blocks.directed: Then he concludes the entire commentary by explaining the final sūtra’s deepest point.

blocks.text: The Śiva-nature of the yogi was not previously absent.
blocks.directed: The Śiva-nature of the yogi was not previously absent.

blocks.text: It was obscured through the self-concealing power of Māyā.
blocks.directed: It was obscured through the self-concealing power of Māyā.

blocks.text: And the practices have brought it to manifestation in recognition. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: And the practices have brought it to manifestation in recognition. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now stop and think about the structure of the whole journey.
blocks.directed: Now stop and think about the structure of the whole journey.

blocks.text: The first sūtra:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The first sūtra:

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: The final sūtra:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The final sūtra:

blocks.text: The inward and outward movements of manifestation are reunited in consciousness.
blocks.directed: The inward and outward movements of manifestation are reunited in consciousness.

blocks.text: We’ve gone from the declaration of the supreme reality to its recognition throughout the entire universe.
blocks.directed: We’ve gone from the declaration of the supreme reality to its recognition throughout the entire universe.

blocks.text: And that is the full movement of the Śiva Sūtras.
blocks.directed: And that is the full movement of the Śiva Sūtras.

blocks.text: Not away from existence.
blocks.directed: Not away from existence.

blocks.text: Not towards an entirely new substance.
blocks.directed: Not towards an entirely new substance.

blocks.text: Not from an independent human being into a separate divine being.
blocks.directed: Not from an independent human being into a separate divine being.

blocks.text: But from misrecognition to recognition.
blocks.directed: But from misrecognition to recognition.

blocks.text: From contraction to the disclosure of freedom.
blocks.directed: From contraction to the disclosure of freedom.

blocks.text: From the limited aṇu to the recognition of the universal Self.
blocks.directed: From the limited aṇu to the recognition of the universal Self.

blocks.text: And the final instruction isn’t:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the final instruction isn’t:

blocks.text: “Destroy the world.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Destroy the world.”

blocks.text: It’s not:
blocks.directed: [short pause] It’s not:

blocks.text: “Suppress every thought.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Suppress every thought.”

blocks.text: It’s not:
blocks.directed: [short pause] It’s not:

blocks.text: “Abandon every relationship.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Abandon every relationship.”

blocks.text: It’s not:
blocks.directed: [short pause] It’s not:

blocks.text: “Become an exceptionally impressive individual.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Become an exceptionally impressive individual.”

blocks.text: It’s something far more radical.
blocks.directed: It’s something far more radical.

blocks.text: Recognise the conscious reality through both the inward withdrawal and outward manifestation of the universe.
blocks.directed: Recognise the conscious reality through both the inward withdrawal and outward manifestation of the universe.

blocks.text: And there’s an exquisite irony here.
blocks.directed: And there’s an exquisite irony here.

blocks.text: Because the whole text has been explaining how to become what, according to the tradition, you never actually ceased to be.
blocks.directed: Because the whole text has been explaining how to become what, according to the tradition, you never actually ceased to be.

blocks.text: You were Śiva.
blocks.directed: You were Śiva.

blocks.text: You experienced limitation.
blocks.directed: You experienced limitation.

blocks.text: You searched for Śiva.
blocks.directed: You searched for Śiva.

blocks.text: You studied Śiva.
blocks.directed: You studied Śiva.

blocks.text: You meditated upon Śiva.
blocks.directed: You meditated upon Śiva.

blocks.text: You worshipped Śiva.
blocks.directed: You worshipped Śiva.

blocks.text: You asked teachers about Śiva.
blocks.directed: You asked teachers about Śiva.

blocks.text: And eventually, the distinction between the seeker and the sought was overcome.
blocks.directed: And eventually, the distinction between the seeker and the sought was overcome.

blocks.text: The ultimate metaphysical hide-and-seek.
blocks.directed: The ultimate metaphysical hide-and-seek.

blocks.text: With one player.
blocks.directed: With one player.

blocks.text: And an infinite number of disguises.
blocks.directed: And an infinite number of disguises.

blocks.text:
THE GRAND FINALE — ALL SEVENTY-SEVEN ŚIVA SŪTRAS
What Vasugupta Actually Just Told Us
Right.
blocks.directed:
THE GRAND FINALE — ALL SEVENTY-SEVEN ŚIVA SŪTRAS
What Vasugupta Actually Just Told Us
Right.

blocks.text: The book is finished.
blocks.directed: The book is finished.

blocks.text: Seventy-seven sūtras.
blocks.directed: Seventy-seven sūtras.

blocks.text: Three sections.
blocks.directed: Three sections.

blocks.text: And an astonishingly unified philosophical argument.
blocks.directed: And an astonishingly unified philosophical argument.

blocks.text: But now that we’ve followed everything, we can finally stand back and see the whole structure.
blocks.directed: But now that we’ve followed everything, we can finally stand back and see the whole structure.

blocks.text: Because there’s something extraordinarily elegant about it.
blocks.directed: Because there’s something extraordinarily elegant about it.

blocks.text: The Śiva Sūtras don’t simply begin with a human being and tell them how to become divine.
blocks.directed: The Śiva Sūtras don’t simply begin with a human being and tell them how to become divine.

blocks.text: They begin by declaring the nature of the divine Self.
blocks.directed: They begin by declaring the nature of the divine Self.

blocks.text: Then they explain why that nature appears concealed.
blocks.directed: Then they explain why that nature appears concealed.

blocks.text: And finally they show how recognition can occur through several distinct modes of practice.
blocks.directed: And finally they show how recognition can occur through several distinct modes of practice.

blocks.text: The movement is not from one independent substance to another.
blocks.directed: The movement is not from one independent substance to another.

blocks.text: It’s from contracted awareness to recognition of its universal nature.
blocks.directed: It’s from contracted awareness to recognition of its universal nature.

blocks.text: And the three upāyas approach this from different standpoints.
blocks.directed: And the three upāyas approach this from different standpoints.

blocks.text:
॥ शिवम् ॥
Iti śivam.
Thus, Śiva. Thus, the auspicious conclusion.
End of the Śiva Sūtras — all 77 sūtras completed.
